record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: Fix an arbitrary probability measure on pure states of a d-dimensional quantum system. Let F(N,M) be the optimal average single-copy fidelity of N-to-M cloning transformations over all M clones, and let F(N,infinity) be the best mean fidelity obtainable by measuring N input copies and repreparing a state from the measurement outcome. Is lim_{M to infinity} F(N,M) always equal to F(N,infinity)? If not for fixed N, does the equality become true in the limit N to infinity?

evidence.quote: Fix an arbitrary probability measure on the pure states of a d-dimensional quantum system. Let F(N, M) be the optimal single copy fidelity for N-to-M cloning transformations, averaged with respect to the given probability measure and over all M clones.

On the other hand, let F(N, ∞) be the best mean fidelity achievable by measuring on N input copies of the state, and repreparing a state according to the measured data. The problem is to decide whether one always gets
lim
M→∞
F(N, M) = F(N, ∞).
A weaker, but still interesting version of the problem is whether the above equation becomes true in the limit N → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H} = \mathbb{C}^d$ be the Hilbert space of a $d$-dimensional quantum system, and fix a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on the set of pure states (equivalently, on the projective space $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{H})$). For positive integers $N \le M$, an $N$-to-$M$ cloning transformation is a completely positive trace-preserving map $T : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}^{\otimes N}) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}^{\otimes M})$. Define the average single-copy cloning fidelity
$$F(N,M) \;=\; \sup_{T} \int \frac{1}{M}\sum_{k=1}^{M} \langle \psi | \, \mathrm{Tr}_{\hat{k}}\!\left(T(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|^{\otimes N})\right) | \psi \rangle \, d\mu(\psi),$$
where $\mathrm{Tr}_{\hat k}$ denotes the partial trace keeping only the $k$-th tensor factor, and the supremum is taken over all such channels $T$.

Define $F(N,\infty)$ as the supremum, over all "measure-and-prepare" (entanglement-breaking) strategies—that is, over all POVMs $\{E_x\}$ on $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes N}$ together with measurable maps $x \mapsto |\phi_x\rangle \in \mathcal{H}$—of the mean fidelity
$$\int \sum_x \mathrm{Tr}\!\left(E_x |\psi\rangle\langle\psi|^{\otimes N}\right) |\langle \phi_x | \psi \rangle|^2 \, d\mu(\psi).$$

Questions:
(a) Is it true that for every $d$, every $N \ge 1$, and every probability measure $\mu$,
$$\lim_{M \to \infty} F(N,M) \;=\; F(N,\infty) \, ?$$
(b) If (a) fails for some fixed $N$, does one nevertheless have
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \Big( \lim_{M \to \infty} F(N,M) - F(N,\infty) \Big) \;=\; 0 \, ?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved affirmatively. Bae and Acín (Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 030402 (2006); arXiv:quant-ph/0603078) proved that optimal $N$-to-$M$ cloning channels become entanglement-breaking (measure-and-prepare) in the limit $M \to \infty$, so that $\lim_{M\to\infty} F(N,M) = F(N,\infty)$ for arbitrary input distributions. Chiribella and D'Ariano subsequently gave quantitative bounds of the form $|F(N,M) - F(N,\infty)| = O(1/M)$. The Open Quantum Problems repository lists this question as solved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic Quantum Cloning Is State Estimation
status_evidence.snippet: Bae and Acín prove that asymptotic cloning is state estimation using monogamy of entanglement and properties of entanglement-breaking channels.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture lim_{M→∞} F(N,M) = F(N,∞) was proved in 2006.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic cloning is state estimation – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Status: Solved. Bae and Acín solved the problem; Chiribella and D'Ariano provided convergence bounds |F(N,M) - F(N,∞)| ≤ c/M.
status_evidence.claim: The Open Quantum Problems database marks this problem as solved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic quantum cloning is state estimation (arXiv:quant-ph/0603078)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the conjecture that asymptotic cloning equals state estimation.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the proof of the equivalence.
